problem: Given that ${y}_{1}(x)={x}^{2}$ is a solution to the equation $2{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-3x{y}^{′}+2y=0$ for $x>0,$ use reduction of order to find a second solution ${y}_{2}(x)$ to the equation, and write down the general solution.
worked_solution:
According to the reduction of order method, we let ${y}_{2}=u(x){x}^{2}.$

Differentiating the above with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{2}^{′} & ={u}^{′}{x}^{2}+2ux \\ {y}_{2}^{″} & ={u}^{″}{x}^{2}+4{u}^{′}x+2u.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}({u}^{″}{x}^{2}+4{u}^{′}x+2u)-3x({u}^{′}{x}^{2}+2ux)+2(u{x}^{2}) & =0 \\ 2{u}^{″}{x}^{4}+8{u}^{′}{x}^{3}+4u{x}^{2}-3{u}^{′}{x}^{3}-6u{x}^{2}+2u{x}^{2} & =0 \\ 2{u}^{″}{x}^{4}+5{u}^{′}{x}^{3} & =0 \\ {x}^{3}(2x{u}^{″}+5{u}^{′}) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${x}^{3}\ne 0$ for $x>0,$ we must have

$$
2x{u}^{″}+5{u}^{′}=0.
$$

Let $w={u}^{′}.$ Then our equation becomes

$$
2x{w}^{′}+5w=0.
$$

This is a separable equation that has the solution

$$
w={c}_{1}{x}^{-5/2}.
$$

But since $w={u}^{′},$ we have

$$
{u}^{′}={c}_{1}{x}^{-5/2}\,⟹\,u=-\frac{2{c}_{1}}{3}{x}^{-3/2}+{c}_{2}.
$$

Hence, our expression for ${y}_{2}(x)=u{x}^{2}$ becomes

$$
{y}_{2}(x)=(-\frac{2{c}_{1}}{3}{x}^{-3/2}+{c}_{2}){x}^{2}.
$$

Setting ${c}_{1}=-\frac{3}{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=0,$ we get

$$
{y}_{2}(x)=({x}^{-3/2}){x}^{2}={x}^{1/2}.
$$

Finally, because $W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})=-\frac{3}{2}{x}^{3/2}\ne 0,$ we know that ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are independent (you should verify this calculation yourself).

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y=A{x}^{2}+B{x}^{1/2}.
$$
